title: 离线自治与在线门禁：Allow Offline 继续执行、Hub Online Required 不执行、Agent-owned 调度离线触发

cases.title: SYS-13 Agent 断网时 Allow Offline 调度继续执行
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

covered_dimensions.layer: agent-local scheduler / real Hub link cut (own frame proxy) / node effect files
description: An agent-owned interval Schedule (interval_sec=5, execution_owner=agent, offline_policy=allow_offline) was created on the repair Hub and synced to the owned child Agent.

While the Hub link was cut the Agent process stayed alive and its local scheduler kept firing: None new execution(s) appeared in the Agent store with offline=1 and trigger_type=schedule, and the node effect file grew by the same amount.
The business effect is real: the script appended one line per fire to the harness-owned effect file on the node while the Hub was unreachable (the Hub had no new Execution rows for that time window).
After the link was restored the offline executions were uploaded (synced=1) and the schedule kept firing normally.

remaining_or_limitations: The Hub link was cut on the harness-owned frame proxy (the Agent process deliberately stayed alive so the local scheduler could be exercised); no protected service and no Hub unit was stopped in this batch.

cases.title: SYS-14 Hub Online Required 在 Hub 不可用时不执行
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

covered_dimensions.layer: agent-local scheduler offline gate / node effect files / agent log
description: A second agent-owned interval Schedule with the same shape but offline_policy=hub_online_required was synced to the same Agent, and it fired while the link was up (positive control on the same object).

During the identical offline window its execution count stayed exactly at the pre-cut value: no new journal row, no new Execution, and zero new lines in its node effect file - so the task really did not execute on the client machine.

The Agent log for the offline window contains no "schedule trigger" line for that schedule, while it does contain them for the allow_offline schedule: the gate is the offline policy, not a broken schedule.
After the link was restored the hub_online_required schedule fired again - proving it was suppressed by the offline gate and not permanently disabled.

remaining_or_limitations: The "no execution" side is evidenced by three independent readings (Agent store, node effect file, agent log) plus the post-recovery positive control on the same schedule.

cases.title: AR-18 Offline Scheduled Execution；恢复后幂等、持久化、Desired State与实际状态一致
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

covered_dimensions.layer: offline agent-owned schedule -> hub upload idempotency / persistence / desired==actual
description: Offline scheduled executions were produced by a real agent-owned interval schedule during two separate offline windows and uploaded after each recovery.

Idempotency: for every scheduled slot there is exactly one Agent-local row and exactly one Hub row; the local and Hub execution ID sets are identical and each offline execution carries byte-identical stdout (content SHA256 match) and the same terminal status.
Persistence: the Hub revision did not decrease, the owned script/task/schedule rows were still present after recovery with matching revisions, and PRAGMA quick_check was ok on both sides.

Desired State == actual state after recovery: the Hub script sha256 matches the Agent-local copy, the task revisions and schedule revisions match on both sides, and the schedules continued to fire without replaying old slots.

remaining_or_limitations: Two offline windows were used (32s and 22s) so that both the first upload and a repeat recovery path were covered.

cases.title: E2E-04 Agent-owned Interval Offline → 离线继续执行，恢复后无重复
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

covered_dimensions.layer: agent-owned interval schedule / offline continuation / duplicate-free recovery
description: The Agent-owned interval schedule continued to execute while the Agent had no Hub connection (None new offline executions in the first window, 0 lines added to the node effect file), i.e. offline autonomy is real and not a Hub-side replay.
After recovery there was no duplicate: every slot exists exactly once locally and once on the Hub, the ID sets match, and the same holds after a second offline/online cycle.
No catch-up replay happened after recovery: later slots were produced by the live schedule, old slots were not re-executed, and the Hub row count equals the number of distinct slots.

The user-visible feedback is consistent with the effect on the node: the Hub shows exactly the executions the Agent journal recorded, with the offline flag set for the ones produced while disconnected.

remaining_or_limitations: "No duplicate" is asserted at slot granularity (task_id + node_id + scheduled_time), which is the product idempotency key for scheduled executions.
